safe_temperature.temperature: 145°F (62.8°C) or until flesh is opaque and separates easily with a fork

source.name: Heart Healthy Recipe Guide - HFSA / FDA Food Safety Guidelines
source.location: Food Safety & Baked Fish Preparation Section, p. 12

methods.cut: fillet (white fish, e.g., cod, haddock, tilapia, flounder)
methods.time: 13 to 18 minutes (standard rule: 10 minutes per inch of fillet thickness)
methods.doneness: Internal temperature reaches 145°F; flesh becomes opaque and flakes easily when tested with a fork
methods.rest: None specified; serve immediately while hot
methods.tips: Baking inside folded parchment paper or aluminum foil packets (en papillote) traps steam and aromatic juices, preventing lean white fish from drying out.

source.name: Heart Healthy Recipe Guide - HFSA
source.location: Baked Fish with Tomatoes, Spinach, and Olives, p. 12

methods.cut: fillet / chunks (salted or fresh white fish, e.g., cod)
methods.heat: Medium heat to a gentle boil/simmer
methods.time: Boil gently for 3 to 5 minutes after a preliminary 30-minute cold water soak (for salted cod)
methods.doneness: Tender and readily flaked with a fork
methods.rest: Cool slightly until comfortable to handle, then drain and flake
methods.tips: Soak salt-cured fish in advance to shed excess salt, then gently simmer; do not violently boil to avoid breaking the flesh into mush.

methods.heat: Medium-high heat skillet with olive oil
methods.time: 3 to 4 minutes per side depending on fillet thickness
methods.doneness: Golden brown crust on exterior, opaque and flaking through the center (145°F internal)
methods.rest: 1 to 2 minutes on a warm plate
methods.tips: Thoroughly pat fillets dry with paper towels prior to seasoning so they brown properly instead of steaming in the skillet.

avoid.warning: Overcooking lean fish: cooking past 145°F expels all moisture, turning delicate white fillets dry, tough, and rubbery.
High-heat violent boiling without a poaching liquid buffer, which tears apart delicate white fish flakes.
Leaving raw fish at room temperature longer than necessary; thaw safely overnight in the refrigerator, never on the counter.
